subject: social-sciences
description: Social Sciences skill tree for CAPS Intermediate Phase (Grades 4–6). Two strands per grade — History (HIS) and Geography (GEO). Map skills topics and History project topics are out of scope for this MCQ-based tutor. Topic IDs preserve the original CAPS term number so they trace cleanly back to the curriculum. Topics do not prerequisite each other — all unlocked from day one.

levels.title: Grade 4 — Social Sciences
levels.description: CAPS Intermediate Phase Grade 4. 4 History topics (one per term) + 3 Geography topics (Term 2 Map skills out of scope). 3 hours/week total. Topics do not prerequisite each other.

atomic_skills.title: Local history
atomic_skills.description: Finding out about the past of a local area through pictures, writing, stories, interviews and objects.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Help the learner think about how we KNOW things about the past. Pictures, stories, objects and writing are all ways. Each gives a different kind of clue.

atomic_skills.title: Learning from leaders
atomic_skills.description: Qualities of good leaders, using Nelson Mandela and Mahatma Gandhi as examples.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Anchor the qualities to specific things the leader did, not vague praise. A good leader serves others, listens, has courage and is willing to sacrifice.

atomic_skills.title: Transport through time
atomic_skills.description: How transport on land, water and in the air has changed over time.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use chronology — old to new. Each invention solved a problem the older one had. Cars are faster than wagons; trains carry more than horses.

atomic_skills.title: Communication through time
atomic_skills.description: How communication has changed over time — from songs, symbols and art to postal systems, radio, telephone, TV, computers and cell phones.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Communication = sharing a message. The TOOLS change, the goal stays the same. Older tools were slower; newer tools reach further faster.

atomic_skills.title: Places where people live (settlements)
atomic_skills.description: Farms, villages, towns and cities; buildings and their uses; landmarks; people's basic needs.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Think about the SIZE and the JOBS. Farms are smallest and most spread out; cities are biggest and have the most kinds of work. A landmark is anything easy to spot.

atomic_skills.title: Food and farming in South Africa
atomic_skills.description: Where food comes from; subsistence vs commercial farming; crop and stock farming in SA; unprocessed and processed foods.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Subsistence = grow to FEED YOUR FAMILY. Commercial = grow to SELL. Processed food has been changed (cooked, dried, ground); unprocessed is as it came from the farm.

atomic_skills.title: Water in South Africa
atomic_skills.description: Uses of water; salt and fresh water; the natural water cycle; how people store and access water; pollution and wastewater.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Water moves in a cycle — sea → cloud → rain → river → sea. We use it, dirty it, and need to clean it before it returns. Salt water is in the sea; fresh water is what we drink.

levels.title: Grade 5 — Social Sciences
levels.description: CAPS Intermediate Phase Grade 5. 4 History topics + 3 Geography topics (Term 1 Map skills out of scope). 3 hours/week total. Topics do not prerequisite each other.

atomic_skills.title: Hunter-gatherers and herders in Southern Africa
atomic_skills.description: San hunter-gatherer society and Khoikhoi herders in the Later Stone Age; how we find out about them; rock art.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The San lived off the land — they HUNTED animals and GATHERED plants. The Khoikhoi kept LIVESTOCK. Both shared the land for thousands of years.

atomic_skills.title: The first farmers in Southern Africa
atomic_skills.description: Bantu-speaking farmers who entered Southern Africa 1700–2000 years ago; homesteads, crops, livestock, iron-working and pottery.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Bantu-speaking farmers brought TWO big new things: farming (crops + cattle) and iron-working. They lived in chiefdoms — not 'tribes' — and shared the land with hunter-gatherers.

atomic_skills.title: An ancient African society: Egypt
atomic_skills.description: Life in ancient Egypt — the Nile, pharaohs, pyramids, hieroglyphics, religion, medicine; Tutankhamen's tomb.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Everything in Egypt started with the Nile — the river made farming possible in the desert. Pharaohs ruled; pyramids were tombs; hieroglyphics were the writing.

atomic_skills.title: A heritage trail through the provinces of South Africa
atomic_skills.description: Examples of heritage from each of the nine provinces — sites, objects, achievements, names, architecture, art and indigenous knowledge.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Heritage = what we inherit from the past. It can be a PLACE (Cradle of Humankind), an OBJECT (gold rhino), a PERSON's work, or an IDEA (indigenous medicine).

atomic_skills.title: Physical features of South Africa
atomic_skills.description: South Africa's landscape — coastal plain, escarpment, plateau; main mountains, rivers and famous features; how human activity changes landscapes.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: South Africa is HIGH in the middle (plateau) and LOW at the coast. Rivers flow from HIGH places down to the sea. The Drakensberg is the highest mountain range.

atomic_skills.title: Weather, climate and vegetation of South Africa
atomic_skills.description: Elements of weather; difference between weather and climate; rainfall patterns; natural vegetation including savannah grasslands.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Weather = TODAY. Climate = the PATTERN over many years. Natural vegetation is plants that grow on their own, shaped by climate.

atomic_skills.title: Minerals and mining in South Africa
atomic_skills.description: SA's main minerals (gold, platinum, diamonds, iron ore, coal); ways of mining; environmental impact; health and safety of miners.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Minerals are non-renewable — once mined, they're gone. SA is famous for gold, platinum and diamonds. Mining can hurt land, air and water, so safety and care matter.

levels.title: Grade 6 — Social Sciences
levels.description: CAPS Intermediate Phase Grade 6. 4 History topics + 3 Geography topics (Term 1 Map skills out of scope). 3 hours/week total. Topics do not prerequisite each other.

atomic_skills.title: An African kingdom long ago: Mapungubwe
atomic_skills.description: Mapungubwe (1220–1300) — first state in Southern Africa; trade across the Indian Ocean; gold objects; Great Zimbabwe; Marco Polo's travels.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mapungubwe was a KINGDOM in the Limpopo Valley — the first big state in Southern Africa. It traded across the Indian Ocean. The famous gold rhino was a symbol of royal power.

atomic_skills.title: Explorers from Europe find Southern Africa
atomic_skills.description: The European Renaissance; new inventions; reasons for exploration; Dias and Da Gama; the VOC.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The Renaissance gave Europe new ideas and tools (compass, caravel). Europeans wanted a sea route to ASIA for trade — and on the way they sailed past Southern Africa.

atomic_skills.title: Democracy and citizenship in South Africa
atomic_skills.description: South Africa's first democratic election in 1994; the Constitution; Parliament; rights and responsibilities; the Constitutional Court; children's rights; national symbols.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Democracy = the people choose their government by voting. South Africa's first FREE election was in 1994. The Constitution is the highest law and protects everyone's rights.

atomic_skills.title: Medicine through time
atomic_skills.description: Indigenous healing in SA; Western scientific discoveries — vaccination (Jenner), germs (Pasteur), TB (Koch), penicillin (Fleming); first heart transplant (Barnard).
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Two ways of healing: indigenous (treats whole person, uses plants and beliefs) and Western (treats the body using science). Both have helped people; today they often work together.

atomic_skills.title: Trade (focus: South Africa and the world)
atomic_skills.description: Why people trade; exports and imports; raw materials vs manufactured goods; fair trade vs unfair trade.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Trade = swapping or selling. EXPORTS go OUT of a country; IMPORTS come IN. Raw materials (cocoa beans) become more valuable when manufactured (chocolate).

atomic_skills.title: Climate and vegetation around the world
atomic_skills.description: Hot, mild and cold climates; tropical rainforests; hot deserts; coniferous forests — climate, vegetation, wildlife and how people live in each.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Climate shapes the plants and animals AND how people live. Rainforests are hot + wet + thick trees. Deserts are hot + dry + few plants. Coniferous forests are cold + tall trees with needles.

atomic_skills.title: Population — why people live where they do
atomic_skills.description: Population distribution and density in SA and the world; reasons for settlement; rural vs urban; rural-to-urban migration.
atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: People settle where life is EASIER — water, good climate, jobs, safety. Cities pull people from the countryside because there's more work. Rural = countryside, urban = city.
